template_records.scope_evidence: The denominator is a bare x=x¹. For every integer a=2..13, subtracting one gives a positive exponent 1..12; a=2 explicitly produces the bare-variable answer. The nonzero condition preserves quotient validity.

A single variable power is raised to another positive integer power. Multiply a∈2..4 by b∈2..5; no coefficient is inside the powered group, so the later power-of-a-product prerequisite is unnecessary.
Apply the nested power to get exponent ab, then the same-base product adds c∈1..2. The family tests the intended order and contains no premature powered coefficient or separate quotient.

The powered product gives coefficient a² and exponent 2c; multiplying by bx gives a²b and exponent 2c+1. Input coefficients 1..2 and output 1..8 are bounded below canonical examples up to 18. This is the intended power-then-product task.

The complete grouped numeric base ax is nonzero, so its zero power is one; in a×x⁰ only x is powered and the outside a remains. A named pair directly tests the authored grouping contrast without introducing an artificial arithmetic combination.
For a∈2..13, reciprocal rule gives 1/a² with positive denominator. Numerator one makes every result already reduced, so the explicitly requested reduced fraction adds no new arithmetic difficulty.
